what.a: {product} is a social media management platform for startups, agencies and brands. You compose a post once, preview it for every platform, check video quality, and schedule it.

quality.q: Why do my videos look blurry after I schedule them?
quality.a: Usually the video does not match what the platform expects, so it gets cropped or re-encoded. Our pre-flight checks warn you before that happens and offer a fix.

ai.a: Yes. The AI assistant in the composer drafts and rewrites captions for each platform, and marks posts made with AI for your team. An API and MCP server for AI agents are coming, with keys limited to one workspace.
ai.aSoon: Soon. AI Studio for images and an AI writer for captions are on the way, with monthly AI credits in every plan. An API and MCP server for AI agents will follow, with keys limited to one workspace.

platforms.q: Which platforms can I post to?
platforms.a: We are building for Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, Facebook, LinkedIn and Bluesky. Each one goes live as soon as that platform approves our app.

safety.q: Is it safe to connect my social accounts?
safety.a: Yes. We connect only through each platform's official sign-in and ask just for the permissions needed to post. Access tokens are encrypted, nothing is posted that you did not schedule, and you can disconnect an account at any time.

trial.q: Do I need a card for the trial?
trial.a: No. You get {days} days with Pro features. When it ends, you move to the Free plan and keep all your data.

cancel.q: Can I cancel at any time?
cancel.a: Yes. Cancel from Billing whenever you like. You keep your plan until the end of the period you paid for, then move to the Free plan. Nothing is deleted.

switch.q: Can I switch from another scheduler?
switch.a: Yes. Import your scheduled posts and media where the other tool allows an export. The first 100 customers get free help moving.

1.title: Add a wide image
1.body: A panorama, or a design made wider than it is tall, works best.

2.title: Choose your slides
2.body: Pick how many slides and their shape, then slide the image to keep the part you want.

3.title: Download and post
3.body: Download the slides and add them to one carousel post, in order from 1.

1.a: Portrait slides are 1080 × 1350 pixels (4:5) and square slides are 1080 × 1080 (1:1). Use one shape for every slide in a post.

2.q: How many slides can I make?
2.a: From 2 to 10, the number Instagram's publishing API takes in one carousel. The Instagram app may allow more.

3.a: Yes. Every slide is cut from the same image with no gap, so the picture carries on as people swipe. Instagram may still compress the images a little.

gridMaker.title: Instagram grid maker
gridMaker.intro: Split one image into 3, 6, 9 or 12 tiles that make one big picture on your profile. Every tile is numbered in the order to post it.
gridMaker.shapeHint: Instagram's profile grid shows posts as tall rectangles (3:4). Choose square if your grid still shows squares.
gridMaker.orderHint: Your newest post shows first, so post tile 1 (bottom right) first and the top-left tile last.

1.title: Add an image
1.body: Use a large one: a 3 × 3 grid of tall tiles needs about 3240 × 4320 pixels to stay sharp.

2.title: Pick rows and shape
2.body: Choose 1 to 4 rows and the tile shape, then move the image to keep the part you want.

3.title: Post in order
3.body: Download the tiles and post them one by one, starting with tile 1.

1.q: Why post the bottom-right tile first?
1.a: Your profile shows the newest post first, in the top left. Posting the bottom-right tile first puts every tile in its place by the end.

2.q: Which tile shape should I use?
2.a: Instagram's profile grid shows posts as 3:4 rectangles, so tall tiles fill each spot. Instagram changes the grid from time to time, so check your profile after the first post.

3.q: Will my grid stay lined up?
3.a: Every later post moves each tile one place along. Post in threes to keep the rows together, and note that pinned posts show first.

1.title: Type a username or a name
1.body: Capitals and the @ are ignored: Instagram usernames are lower case.

2.title: Check the rules
2.body: Up to 30 letters, numbers, periods and underscores, with no period at the start or end and no two in a row.

3.title: See if it's free
3.body: Open the profile address. If a profile appears, the name is taken; if not, it may be free.

1.q: Can this tool tell me if a username is free?
1.a: No. Instagram offers no public way to check, and we do not scrape it. Open the profile link: if a profile appears, the name is taken.

2.q: What can an Instagram username contain?
2.a: Letters, numbers, periods and underscores, up to 30 characters. Spaces, accents and other symbols are not allowed.

3.q: Why is a name that looks free refused?
3.a: Instagram can also hold back names, for example ones used by accounts that were closed. If a name is refused, try one of the ideas.

3.q: Should my TikTok and Instagram usernames match?
3.a: It helps people find you. TikTok allows 24 characters and Instagram 30, so a name that works on both has 24 or fewer. Check it with both checkers.
